summary.en-US: EPUB reader for newspaper and magazine issues, fetched from your own drive

description.en-US:
Opens an issue as a contents page — one card per article, by section — then each
article on its own page, with previous / contents / next always on top. Made for
daily EPUB issues on e-ink: new issues are fetched from a folder on your own drive (a
kDrive share link or any WebDAV server), so a daily script can drop the papers there.
Ordinary books open as in Book's Story, which it forks.

summary.en-US: Black-and-white e-book reader: pages, not scrolling; WebDAV library

description.en-US:
Channels, episodes, favourites, downloads: four plain lists, no artwork. Feeds are
added by pasting or sharing a link, and an episode resumes where you stopped. It can
be transcribed and translated on the phone, and read while it plays; transcripts can
go to your Reader's Books library over WebDAV. No directory,
no recommendations, no account: OPML and one settings file are the whole sync with
the desktop twin.

summary.en-US: Black-and-white voice recorder, transcribed on the phone, optional WebDAV sync

description.en-US:
One tap records a memo, a lecture or a conversation, screen off included. The phone
itself writes the transcript (whisper.cpp), evens the loudness and can list the main
points (beta) — by default nothing leaves it. Optionally, recordings and transcripts
are synced with your own WebDAV folder (kDrive, Nextcloud…), where your own computer
can transcribe in the phone's place. Text only, six languages.

summary.en-US: Scans to searchable PDFs, text read on the phone, WebDAV copy

description.en-US:
A map for cycling, hiking and public transport in Switzerland, in the spirit of the old
GPS boxes: one screen, big buttons, the official hiking trails, cycling routes and
public-transport lines in their signpost colours on the swisstopo map. Routing runs on
the phone (BRouter, OpenStreetMap data), through as many stops as you like, previewed
before you start (distance, time, climb, the streets taken, every turn with its street
name), then turn-by-turn guidance that goes on with the screen off; your own tours (GPX,
KML, GeoJSON, TCX, FIT files, or recorded) are kept and followed as they are, and
the signposted routes of SwitzerlandMobility (on foot, barrier-free, bike, mountain bike) are
listed nearest first, offline. Public transport: the next
journeys to your stop, drawn leg by leg, then guidance in big letters (walk, board, get
off, change) with real-time timetables online and an optional offline timetable of all
Switzerland. What is around you, offline: drinking water, shelters, huts, fire places,
bike shops, bakeries, cafés, restaurants, shops, practices, firms… from OpenStreetMap, searched by
category or name (with a town: « Ardentis Lausanne ») in one search with addresses, stops and favourites, shown on the map, each with its card (open now, hours, phone, add to
contacts). The firms of the Swiss commercial register, offline (about 789 000, at their
registered address), and the address of one of your contacts through Android's picker.
Favourites, people and firms looked up
on search.ch in a browser tab, one button putting the entry on the map; a night map, and the whole country saved offline in one button. A route planner
on every map (start, destination, date and time, share, keep). Six languages. No
account, no tracking: the network serves the map tiles, the downloads and searches you
ask for, and the transit map sends your position to transport.opendata.ch to find the
stops around you.
